title: What AI Actually Is: Module Quiz

cards.prompt: Does each one **follow rules** someone wrote, or **learn from examples**?

items.label: An online shop's "you might like" list

cards.explanation: A microwave timer and a spreadsheet's adding follow exact rules. Turning speech into text and suggesting things you might like have endless variety, so they **learn from examples**.

cards.prompt: The model calls the mini basketball a tennis ball. Choose which examples to train on, so it gets **every** test ball right.
cards.explanation: Every basketball the model learned from was big, so the mini one sat closer to the tennis balls. Adding the **small basketball** shows it that basketballs can be small too. Taking the tennis balls out would break the tennis ball test.

cards.prompt: A model learned to spot dogs from photos taken **only in daylight**. What will it most likely get wrong?

options.text: The photos it was trained on
Dogs in photos taken at night
Nothing: the kind of photos doesn't matter

cards.explanation: A model only knows what it was shown. It never saw a dog at night, so night photos are where it will slip up, like the yellow apple. Adding night photos to its training data would help.

cards.prompt: Put the steps of teaching a computer in order, from first to last.
cards.explanation: Collect, label, train, test, then use. Testing on new examples before using a model shows how often it gets things wrong.

cards.prompt: You're writing a report on volcanoes with an AI helper.

steps.text: The AI confidently tells you the highest volcano in the world. Your report will be marked. What do you do?

choices.consequence: It might be right, but it might not. AI answers are predictions, and confidence doesn't make them true.

choices.text: Check it in a trusted source first
choices.consequence: Exactly: important facts get checked with a source you trust.

choices.text: Ask the AI to promise it's right
choices.consequence: It may well promise, but it can't be sure its own answer is right, so a promise doesn't make it true.

cards.explanation: An AI's answer is a prediction. For anything important, **check it with a trusted source** before you rely on it.

cards.prompt: Match each word to what it means.

pairs.right: What the computer builds to guess

cards.explanation: **Training data** is the examples; a **label** says what each example really is; the **model** is what the computer builds from them; and a **prediction** is its best guess about something new.
